# `Q-18-2` — Engine Include File Could Not Be Read

> An execution engine asked Quarto to include the contents of a file in
> the output, but the file could not be read; the render continues
> without it.

## What this means

Engines can hand Quarto extra content to place in the document header,
before the body, or after the body. knitr uses this to deliver the
`<script>` and `<link>` tags an HTML dependency needs — for example the
JavaScript and CSS behind an htmlwidget. The engine writes that content
to a temporary file and tells Quarto where it is.

This warning means one of those files could not be read. Quarto skips
it and keeps rendering, so the page is produced, but whatever that file
carried is missing: a widget may appear as an empty box, a stylesheet
may not apply, a script may not run.

## Why this happens

- The temporary directory the engine wrote to was cleaned up before
  Quarto read it (an aggressive temp cleaner, or a tool that removes
  the render's working directory mid-run).
- The engine reported a path relative to a directory Quarto is not
  running in.
- File permissions prevent Quarto from reading the file.

## How to fix

The message names the path that could not be read and the reason the
operating system gave.

1. Re-run the render. A transient cleanup race usually does not recur.
2. If it recurs, check the named path: does it exist, and is it readable
   by the user running Quarto?
3. If the path looks wrong (relative, or in a directory Quarto never
   created), this is a bug in the engine integration — report it at
   <https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/issues> with the full warning
   text.

Use `--strict` to make this warning stop the render instead of
producing a page with missing content:

```bash
q2 render --strict
```
